name: Western Marxism
summary: Western Marxism is the non-Soviet current of Marxist theory that grew after the failed revolutions in the West around 1918-23. It shifts attention from economics and party strategy to philosophy, culture, consciousness and domination, drawing on Hegel and humanist Marx. Its thinkers criticise reification, the culture industry and technological rationality, remain anti-capitalist, and disagree about parties, revolution and the prospects of the working class.
scope: The tradition from Lukács (History and Class Consciousness, 1923), Korsch and Gramsci (Prison Notebooks) through the Frankfurt School (Horkheimer, Adorno, Marcuse, Benjamin, later Habermas). Sartre, Lefebvre and Althusser are named in the literature as members but are weighted less. Soviet Marxism-Leninism, Trotskyism and Maoism are excluded; where the strand splits, such as on the vanguard party, the answer is neutral.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Western Marxists wrote little on health policy; as anti-capitalists they would back decommodified care, though Marcuse-style critics also saw welfare provision as integrating workers into the system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a topic of the tradition; a reform that eases workers' conditions is acceptable, but the tradition treats wage labour itself as the problem rather than its level.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Lukács's commodity-fetishism analysis and Marcuse's critique of market 'free competition at administered prices' reject the idea that markets rationally serve human needs.

public-ownership.rationale: Anti-capitalist theorists favour social ownership of major industry, but the tradition rarely discusses nationalisation and distrusts bureaucratic state administration, so support is moderate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Consistent with opposition to capitalist inequality, but the tradition offers no fiscal programme and regards redistribution as insufficient reform.

unions-good.rationale: Gramsci backed the Turin factory-council movement and Frankfurt theorists sought unity with the oppressed, though Marcuse doubted that organised labour still opposed the system.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of the means of production underlies the reification and domination the tradition attacks, so a near-inviolable property right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Marcuse saw managerial corporate rule as domination turned into administration; regulation might help but leaves the system intact, and adherents prefer transformation to regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Adherents oppose cuts that hurt workers, even though Marcuse argued the welfare state helps integrate them; dependency arguments belong to the opposing camp.

worker-ownership.rationale: Gramsci's praise of the Turin councils as a movement of workers 'founders of a state' and the council communist roots of Lukács and Korsch point to worker control of production.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Critical theory's picture of 'totally administered lives' makes adherents wary of state surveillance, though the point is inferred rather than discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; Marcuse's emphasis on liberation from repressive social control suggests a permissive lean, but the stance is inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Marcuse defended 'repressive tolerance' and restricting regressive movements, while others in the tradition stress free critique; the issue splits adherents.

strong-leader.rationale: The tradition stresses mass self-education and critical autonomy and studied authoritarianism as a pathology, so leaders bypassing democratic process is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Western Marxists distrust the state as a site of domination, but Gramsci treats it as a terrain to be contested and none embrace anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; a left-critical tradition might lean to restriction but also values popular armed struggle historically, so it is split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from critical theory's wariness of administered coercion and its anti-fascist stance; police and military funding is not discussed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marcuse's sexual liberation thesis favours legalisation, while Marxist critics of commodification see it as reified labour; unaddressed and split.

decide-locally.rationale: Council democracy points toward local, grassroots decision-making, but Gramsci's national hegemonic bloc and internationalism cut the other way.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from Frankfurt School work on the social causes of domination and a humanist view of persons; penal policy is not a main topic.

traditional-family.rationale: Frankfurt theorists analysed the authoritarian family as a site where domination is reproduced, so they do not treat traditional family structures as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Marcuse's sexual liberation themes and the left-liberationist current; the tradition did not address marriage rights directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's emancipatory, anti-repressive orientation; no source here states a position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is treated as part of ideology and common sense that critique must question, but Gramsci also took religion seriously as popular culture; the stance is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Critical theory studied racism and antisemitism as products of domination and aims at emancipation, which implies active correction of injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Critical theory's view that character and needs are socially shaped supports the claim, though gender itself is not a focus of the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Gramsci engaged with national-popular culture, but the tradition mainly seeks class-based and internationalist culture rather than preserving national traditions.

gradual-change.rationale: Frankfurt critical theory rejected social-democratic reformism, and Gramsci's long 'war of position' is a strategy for transformation, not respect for existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and studied scapegoating of minorities as a release valve for social rage; restriction is opposed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Adherents are internationalist but critics of capitalist institutions such as the UN-led order; unaddressed in the sources.

free-trade.rationale: The commodity-form critique makes adherents sceptical that free trade benefits everyone, though the tradition has no developed trade theory.

nation-first.rationale: An internationalist, class-based tradition rejects putting national interest above global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and anti-militarism; a mixed picture because anti-fascist tradition accepts force against fascism.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalism points that way, but 'eventually open' is not a stated programme in the sources, so the support is inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Marcuse and Horkheimer-Adorno criticise domination of nature and consumerism, which suggests sympathy, while the tradition also demands material abundance for all.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Critique of the domination of nature in Dialectic of Enlightenment suggests support, but climate policy as such is anachronistic for the founders.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Dialectic of Enlightenment and Marcuse argue that technological rationality becomes an instrument of domination; the sources explicitly reject technological salvation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; critics of technocratic domination and ecological sceptics are wary, but no stated position exists.

revolution-justified.rationale: Lukács and Gramsci were revolutionary communists, and Marcuse looked to a 'Great Refusal'; revolution is sometimes justified, though later theorists were pessimistic about it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Critical theory attacks technocracy and positivist science as serving domination, and Habermas defends a robust public sphere.

central-planning.rationale: Traditionally socialist but the tradition rejected Soviet-style planning and wrote little on economics, so adherents are split.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not address market socialism; adherents are split between planned and worker-run market forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: A Georgist single tax is a liberal reform alien to a tradition seeking abolition of capitalist property relations; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Consistent with anti-capitalist egalitarianism but not discussed in these sources.

basic-income.rationale: Marcuse's vision of freedom from toil is sympathetic, yet integrationist concerns about welfare handouts divide adherents.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Internationalist anti-capitalism does not favour protecting domestic capital; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Socialist tradition favours collective direction of investment but Western Marxists distrust state bureaucracy; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The tradition seeks to overcome private property in production, not spread it, though it did not target small owners directly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Marx's horizon of abolishing wage labour is retained, and Lukács's analysis of abstract, quantified labour makes wage labour the core of reification, though few Western Marxists stress money abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A market-libertarian demand opposed to the tradition's anti-capitalism; inferred from its socialist orientation.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Critical theory analysed state-corporatist and fascist arrangements as forms of domination, and rejected both social-democratic and state-capitalist management of labour.

one-party-rule.rationale: Western Marxism defined itself against Soviet orthodoxy and Frankfurt theorists rejected Moscow-aligned communism; a single ruling party is opposed.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is incompatible with the tradition's emancipatory, egalitarian orientation; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Marcuse said 'free election of masters does not abolish the masters', while Habermas defends democracy strongly; adherents are split on democracy as an unqualified good.

direct-votes.rationale: Council and participatory traditions favour direct popular decision-making, though the sources do not discuss referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Gramsci praised the Turin council movement and Lukács and Korsch came from council communism, but later Frankfurt theorists dropped the idea, so support is moderate.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; Gramsci's national-popular concerns and internationalism leave no clear answer.

natural-rulers.rationale: Gramsci's organic intellectuals and the critique of ideology treat ruling status as socially produced, and the tradition is egalitarian.

political-violence-never.rationale: Gramsci and Lukács accepted revolutionary force, though later critical theorists were reluctant about violence; it is not never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: The tradition is anti-militarist and the Frankfurt School analysed the authoritarian personality; glorifying war is rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: Left-Hegelian critique of religion is an origin of the tradition and secular politics is assumed, but strict separation is not a stated plank.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secular, critical tradition roots law in human emancipation, not scripture; inferred from its Left-Hegelian origins.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A libertarian proposal opposed to the tradition's critique of commodification; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-militarist and internationalist; superiority over rivals is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Critical theory studied ethnic nationalism and antisemitism as pathologies of domination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle remains central, yet Western Marxists emphasised consciousness, culture and totality over economic determinism, so the answer is agree rather than strongly agree.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Marcuse's critique of toil and false needs favours substantive equality, though the sources do not discuss equality of outcomes as such.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial and emancipatory commitments; not discussed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; Western Marxists wrote little on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and class-based, not civilisational, solidarity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Lukács and Marcuse attack bourgeois individualism and heteronomous needs, so pursuing self-interest as a moral good is rejected.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Critical theory retains the Kantian ideal of autonomy while criticising its individualist form, so it does not subordinate individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Dialectic of Enlightenment criticises domination of nature, suggesting sympathy, but humanist Marxism centres human emancipation; split.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists traditionally reject Malthusian explanations of poverty; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Kulturkritik and Dialectic of Enlightenment are sharply critical of industrial modernity, but the tradition is not anti-industrial and wants its fruits shared.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological rationality is seen as a vehicle of domination in advanced capitalism, so accelerating change for its own sake is rejected.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from critique of instrumental reason and domination of inner nature.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Horkheimer and Adorno's warning that thought becomes an automatic process replaceable by machines makes algorithmic government a case of reified reason.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from opposition to administered, surveilled life; not discussed.

restore-past-order.rationale: The tradition is progressive and emancipatory, though its Kulturkritik also laments loss; restoring an old order is not its goal.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Critical theory insists on theory-guided critique and rejects positivist neutrality, so judging policies without ideology is resisted.

direct-action.rationale: Gramsci favoured a party-led long war of position and Adorno doubted activism, while Marcuse backed movement politics; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Frankfurt theorists held that practice must not reproduce domination, but Lukács and Gramsci accepted instrumental party discipline; unclear.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Even critics of domination of nature seek emancipation through modern society, not abandoning civilisation.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's classical aim persists and Lukács attacks specialised, fragmented labour, but the sources do not centre it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marcuse's distinction of true and false needs and the Marxian aim of a society serving human needs fit this principle, though it is not stated as a slogan.

production-for-use.rationale: Lukács diagnoses the commodity form as producing for exchange, and Marcuse seeks production oriented to true needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The tradition inherits Marx's analysis but Anderson notes its 'studied silence' on economics, so it is accepted rather than developed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lukács and Gramsci accepted the idea in the early 1920s, but council communists and Frankfurt theorists distanced themselves; split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pollock, Marcuse and others tied capitalism to imperialism, but Western Marxists mostly avoided economic theory of war; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: A libertarian claim wholly alien to the tradition; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Marcuse's critique of liberal tolerance and 'repressive' freedoms means restricting the state to preventing harm is seen as too thin.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Habermas and the tradition value individual autonomy but critique abstract individualism; group claims are not ruled out.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A market-style claim opposed to the tradition's emphasis on collective, democratic self-determination.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers is reification of social relations as commodity relations.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marcuse distinguishes real freedom from merely formal choice, holding that choice among goods is not freedom if they sustain alienation; freedom requires material and social means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Critical theory stresses the culture industry's power but holds ultimate power lies with capital, not universities and media over elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Critical theory studied racist ideology and the authoritarian personality as social products; genetic hierarchy is firmly rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist and organic representation is analysed in the tradition as part of fascist domination.

total-state.rationale: Dialectic of Enlightenment and the 'totally administered' society critique are explicitly anti-totalitarian.

national-rebirth.rationale: Palingenetic nationalism is studied by the tradition as an element of fascism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal fealty contradicts the democratic emancipatory orientation.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is the kind of unfree labour the tradition's liberation project opposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Horkheimer's 'Traditional and Critical Theory' argues positivist science is tied to practical interests, and Gramsci links ideas to class struggle, so knowledge is not neutral.

universal-morality.rationale: Habermas defends universalist morality, but the tradition's historicism and critique of Enlightenment reason make adherents mostly sceptical; split in the strand.

single-common-good.rationale: Gramsci and Marxism see society as divided by class interests that are not reconcilable by pure reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Frankfurt thinkers varied.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; adherents unlikely to have a settled view.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist project the sources never discuss, and the tradition's class focus offers no stance; neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Council traditions and the Turin movement support democratic control in workplaces.

school-vouchers.rationale: Gramsci stressed schools as hegemonic institutions and a public, unified education; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Austerity orthodoxy is not favoured by a left tradition; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marcuse says liberty can become 'a powerful instrument of domination' under a repressive whole, and rejects market freedom as a basis of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule by moral example of rulers is a Confucian idea absent from the tradition; inferred from its democratic orientation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Gramsci took national questions seriously but the tradition is internationalist; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Critical theory criticises instrumental reason and treats Enlightenment as turning into myth, but retains emancipatory reason and Left-Hegelian secularism; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Internationalism and universal solidarity oppose citizenship-restricted welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Marcuse's critique of toil and false needs makes compulsory work conditions unattractive.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class conflict and counter-hegemony are central, and Frankfurt theorists rejected social-democratic reformism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Western Marxists such as Adorno and Benjamin prized inherited culture; Futurist iconoclasm is not their view.

workers-nation.rationale: Internationalist class organisation is the norm.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Critical theory critiques authoritarian family structure and patriarchal domination; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Marxist critique targets capital relations broadly, not interest bans, which are not discussed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racism is analysed throughout the tradition as domination; racial segregation is firmly rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Gramsci's civil society and hegemony view treats the state as more than a tool of force, and Western Marxists neglected or complicated the instrumental view; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from critique of domination of nature and capital-driven growth.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The tradition is wary of forced homogenisation and studies scapegoating of minorities.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claims of this type are studied as scapegoating by Frankfurt authors.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral-system design is not discussed in the sources, and adherents' preference for councils over parliaments gives no ranking of electoral rules.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperialist; spreading a national model is rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from Frankfurt analysis of the authoritarian family and Marcuse's critique of repression; limited discussion.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Western Marxism analyses structural domination rather than individual corruption claims.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is part of the biological racism the Frankfurt tradition opposes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from anti-authoritarian and anti-fascist stance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The minimal state defended by liberal market theorists is opposed to the tradition's critique of liberty under a repressive whole.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kantian autonomy and human emancipation are retained by critical theory, though adherents view formal legal equality as insufficient.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Western Marxism arose after post-war revolutions failed in the West and rejected the Soviet model; Lukács and Gramsci's internationalism fits, though the thesis is not discussed explicitly.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Western Marxist sources here say nothing on settler states, and anti-imperial sympathies pull against the strand's silence; neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are outside the sources; secular universalism and respect for minorities point in opposite directions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Emancipatory and secular orientation implies freedom of conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred; the tradition has no religious-law politics.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Gramsci saw schools as hegemonic; secular schooling is consistent with Left-Hegelian secularism, but unaddressed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Western Marxists criticised Soviet statism and expected the state to be overcome; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Gramsci's hegemony emphasises consent and Habermas stresses democratic legitimacy, though the tradition adds that consent can be manufactured.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is not endorsed by an internationalist tradition.

population-transfer.rationale: Studies of persecution of minorities; rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian non-aggression principle conflicts with revolutionary justification of force and property critique.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition is treated as an expression of commodity society's reification and 'free competition at administered prices'.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Marcuse favoured repressing regressive movements while liberal critics oppose; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The tradition's emphasis on domination fits the claim, though the republican formulation is not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed as such; Habermas supports it and Marxists have long criticised liberal checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lukács and Gramsci championed the party as organiser of consciousness, while Luxemburg-influenced and Frankfurt currents rejected Leninist obedience; the strand is split.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Anti-capitalist and emancipatory, though the sources do not frame it as a law-making principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A privatising measure alien to socialist housing policy; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The tradition supports workers' collective action.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxists attribute poverty to social institutions, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Rejected as scapegoating by critical theory.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; participatory sympathies are offset by lack of any stated view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Critical theory analysed emergency rule in Nazi state and condemned administered coercion.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes Soviet-style control and wrote on how media pacify; state or party control is rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Soviet-style party-state.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Reflects council and Paris Commune tradition, not directly stated in sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lukács and Gramsci prized party discipline, but Luxemburg and Frankfurt currents rejected 'blind obedience'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Habermas is pro-European, while others see the EU as capitalist; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Strong executive power over the military is incompatible with democratic and anti-authoritarian commitments.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a concern; inferred from secular orientation.

clerical-rule.rationale: Theocracy is wholly opposed to the secular Left-Hegelian origin of the tradition.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's defeatism was Soviet-centered; Western Marxists were split and the sources do not state it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adorno defends autonomous art that refuses reconciliation, so moral censorship is rejected.

recall-officials.rationale: Council democracy with removable delegates; inferred from the Turin and council tradition.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The sources discuss no alliance policy; anti-militarism and anti-fascist alliance traditions leave adherents split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a programme of this tradition and conflicts with socialised housing.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not a theme; the tradition is urban-industrial in focus.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The national-division question is not treated by these theorists, who centred class over national borders.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Gramsci's organic intellectuals show that educated people can serve the working class, rejecting anti-intellectual populism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Critical theory criticises Eurocentrism, but Dialectic of Enlightenment holds a progress narrative; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Critical theory criticises positivism but not for religious replacement of science; creationism is rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Marcuse's 'repressive desublimation' critiques commercial sexuality while he also opposed sexual repression; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic criteria for membership are rejected.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; secular egalitarianism and protection of minorities pull in different directions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Marcuse and Adorno defend non-conformity against one-dimensional society.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Gramsci and council theorists prized popular self-organisation, but none of the sources addresses constituent assemblies specifically.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents value democracy but have no view on this institutional design.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Insulating monetary policy from elected government sits poorly with a tradition critical of administrative rule and capital power; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property is held to be justified only in social terms; the tradition goes further and aims at overcoming it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Western Marxists broadly rejected Soviet orthodoxy and Pollock theorised state capitalism, but adherents differ on exactly how to label the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from critique of instrumental reason and domination of nature.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; secular but wary of state power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A ceremonial unifying head of state is not a question the tradition addressed, and the answer is left neutral.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and self-determination sympathies.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The tradition's secular, Left-Hegelian origin rejects sacral rulership outright.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The sources are silent on one-country-two-systems autonomy arrangements.

character-from-environment.rationale: Critical theory and Marcuse treat needs and character as socially and historically formed; Marcuse says needs are 'historical needs'.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler exempt from law contradicts the tradition's anti-authoritarian and democratic commitments, though it is inferred rather than debated.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from scepticism about technological progress as a goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not engaged by Western Marxists, whose sources never rank forms of government this way.

leader-cult.rationale: Studied as a feature of authoritarian domination.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is outside the sources, and adherents have no common view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Western Marxists rarely engaged this Maoist thesis; split.

land-redistribution.rationale: Gramsci analysed the failure to mobilise peasants against landowners, supporting redistribution, though it is not their main topic.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Left-Hegelian secular critique of religion firmly rejects punishing apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes are repression that the tradition opposes.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not addressed; critics of European capitalism and pro-EU Habermasians split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Austro-Marxist proposal is not discussed in the sources used, so no stance can be fairly attributed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources give no view on diaspora strategy, though internationalism leans toward fighting locally; left neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Western Marxists emphasised consciousness, culture and philosophy over economic determinism; Gramsci insisted on the economy's role but gave ideas real force.

ban-cartels.rationale: Marcuse viewed monopoly capitalism as structural, so restoring competition is not the answer.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposition to bailouts could come from anti-capitalist or from market sympathies, and the sources never address it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Critical theory retains rights as safeguards against domination.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic bloc is a fascist-era policy analysed critically.

moral-incentives.rationale: Marcuse's critique of false needs sympathises, but Western Marxists did not endorse Guevarist incentives; split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Gramsci held that revolution requires hegemony and a long war of position, and later theorists doubted voluntarist action.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Critics note the Frankfurt analysis of Enlightenment as domination and anti-colonial sympathies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Studies of authoritarian personality oppose conformist loyalty education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from commitment to correct racial injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the sources and adherents have no shared line.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Frankfurt theorists and Marcuse argued advanced capitalism integrates opposition and adapts, causing pessimism about collapse (Anderson's pessimism noted by Wikipedia).

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marcuse argued workers in rich countries are integrated into the system, but not by the 'labor aristocracy' thesis per se; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Habermas defends constitutional rights while Marxist critics call them bourgeois; the strand is split and the sources are silent.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-imperial sympathies suggest sympathy, but no source here addresses colonial treaty law.

minority-veto.rationale: Collective discipline and democratic majorities; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Council tradition prefers councils to parliaments but Gramsci engaged parliaments; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Frankfurt School's domination-of-nature critique includes concern for suffering; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed; the domination-of-nature critique and ordinary humane practice conflict.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity from privilege reinforces hegemony rather than changing structures.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition insists on praxis and engagement, though Adorno withdrew into theory in places.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Horkheimer and Adorno's culture industry argues mass culture numbs critical capacities and reconciles audiences to the status quo.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramsci's cultural hegemony holds that rulers maintain power through consent spread by schools, churches and media, as complement to force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not a Western Marxist focus; dependency theory is another strand.

party-own-road.rationale: Western Marxism arose against Comintern direction, which attacked Lukács and Korsch.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is outside the sources and adherents have no common position.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources do not address indigenous political leadership, and egalitarian and anti-colonial commitments conflict on it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Critical theory was formed in response to fascism and studied authoritarianism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Frankfurt theorists criticised both Stalinism and fascism but treat fascism as a product of capitalism; adherents split on equivalence.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the strand has no shared view.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the strand has no shared view.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Critical theory has universalist elements; postcolonial critique of Eurocentrism splits the strand.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligation is discussed only in critiques of the authoritarian family, giving no clear position on filial duty.

office-by-exam.rationale: The civil-service exam system is outside the sources and the tradition takes no side.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism and internationalism conflict, and the sources do not address investment screening.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Council and Turin traditions held delegates accountable to those who chose them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatisation of social insurance rejected; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal tenure resembles socialist ownership, but the sources do not take up usufruct land systems.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is a liberal constitutional point on which the council-oriented tradition has no stated view.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Structural analysis of domination implies it, though not stated.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Marcuse says most needs to behave and consume in accordance with advertisements are false needs which perpetuate toil and repression, producing 'euphoria in unhappiness'.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-imperialism rejects covert intervention by great powers, though solidarity with leftist insurgents might invite exceptions; the sources are silent.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pronatalist policy is not discussed; anti-nativist views conflict with support for family subsidies.

residents-only-property.rationale: Housing restriction is not addressed; anti-speculation sympathies conflict with internationalism.

job-guarantee.rationale: Consistent with socialist orientation but unaddressed.

democratic-peace.rationale: Critical theory doubts liberal democratic progress narratives.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Critical theory questions legitimacy but the sources do not state whether a general duty to obey exists.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism favours non-intervention while anti-fascism supports it in some cases; the tradition does not settle this.

industrial-unions.rationale: Gramsci's factory council movement organised by workplace; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Frankfurt School studied antisemitism as a release valve for social rage, not as truth.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The sources discuss critique of the family but do not call for abolishing legal marriage, so adherents are split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Habermas's public sphere emphasises transparency; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not a theme of the tradition, which accepts industrial production on a large scale.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gramsci stressed organisation and the party; the tradition rarely endorses informal anarchist structures.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A tributary order of ritual deference is incompatible with the internationalist, egalitarian outlook, inferred without direct discussion.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Classical Marxist distinction retained, though Western Marxists did not restate it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Opposes anti-communism as a project while criticising Soviet communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mixed provision is a social-democratic design the Frankfurt School criticised as reformism, but no source addresses service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: Left-Hegelian origins treat religion as ideology, but Gramsci took religion seriously as common sense and the Frankfurt School less dismissive; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism recognises capitalism's historic role, but the Western strand emphasised its reification and domination more than its progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-capitalist analysis suggests it, though gender is not central to the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty questions with internal nations are not covered by the sources used.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Council sympathies conflict with Gramsci's emphasis on national hegemony; split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Western Marxists reject Soviet communism but remain anti-capitalist, so a 'third course' framing of equal rejection is mostly refused.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Frankfurt School's founding concerns include Nazi genocide and antisemitism; denial is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law duty is outside the tradition's secular framework and not discussed in sources.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Gramsci praised councils as masses made 'founders of a state' and Habermas defends public deliberation; ordinary people deciding for themselves fits the tradition.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Critical theory analyses multiple forms of domination; intersectionality is later.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical ethics is not covered by the sources, and adherents have no shared line.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Critical theory remains committed to the left project.

alienated-labor.rationale: Lukács describes labour under commodity production as abstract and quantified, absorbing workers into mechanical systems, and Western Marxism built on the 1844 Manuscripts' humanist theory of alienation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Secularist and minority-rights commitments conflict, and the sources do not address the question.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarism points toward it, but revolutionary and anti-fascist traditions defend armed force; the sources do not address abolition.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Western Marxism positioned itself between Soviet and Western orthodoxies but did not address foreign policy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit is a different socialist current and not discussed by Western Marxists in these sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Gramsci and the councils sought mass participation; exclusion of the propertyless is opposed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Marcuse argued corporate managers and technocratic administration dominate national government and purpose, so corporate influence over government is excessive.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-imperialist orientation rejects cultivating influence over former imperial domains.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking is a dependency-theory proposal that Western Marxists did not address; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Western Marxism defined itself against Soviet orthodoxy, and the Comintern's attacks on Lukács and Korsch illustrate its opposition to bloc discipline imposed from above.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-capitalist; colonial extraction is rejected.

reification.rationale: Reification is the central concept of Lukács's History and Class Consciousness and was extended by the Frankfurt School.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Adorno and Horkheimer tie domination of nature to domination of people and Marcuse to liberation of both; women specifically are less central, so this is inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The culture-industry and false-needs critiques hold that formal freedoms are emptied when capital controls media and public expression.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Frankfurt thinkers valued legal guarantees against arbitrary power but distrusted formal legality as a cover for domination; the strand is split.

racial-franchise.rationale: The tradition's humanist and emancipatory core, and Frankfurt studies of authoritarianism, oppose race-based exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Habermas favours public deliberation while Marcuse-style critics fear technology integrating people into the system.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Habermas's publicity ideal and the critique of administration; the tradition does not address records directly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The tradition's critique of authoritarian and communal domination opposes legal limits on adults' marriage choices.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Frankfurt analyses of prejudice and antisemitism treat such shunning as a mark of the authoritarian personality.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Gramsci's and Lukacs's stress on mass self-government and Habermas's deliberation; the tradition never discussed sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marxist critique of religion coexists with Benjamin's and Bloch's use of theology; the strand is split and the issue marginal.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: As anti-capitalist critics of domination and reification, Western Marxists hold that concentrated private wealth distorts society and subordinates people to it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from Marcuse's call for sexual liberation and the tradition's critique of repression; the specific issue of military service is not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Critical theorists criticised religion as ideology but did not call for state-imposed atheism, which would reproduce domination; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Gramsci analysed the police as part of the coercive state, but the tradition did not propose their abolition, and its thinkers differ.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The tradition did not address consociational arrangements, and its thinkers differ on democratic form.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Marcuse and others saw welfare provision as integrating workers in the system, and charity as a symptom of inequality; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the tradition, and its thinkers differ on representative institutions.

vote-delegation.rationale: Gramsci backed council democracy and recallable delegates, but per-policy delegation of votes is not discussed and thinkers differ.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The tradition criticised technological rationality, but extinction risk as a policy priority is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the critique of domination and patriarchy in Critical Theory; religious office is not a documented topic.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Frankfurt School studied the authoritarian family as a site of domination, so shared marital authority is implied; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Western Marxism's humanist, anti-capitalist universalism, which favours widening inclusion; the tradition did not address local voting.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its critique of the commodification of necessities such as housing; the tradition wrote little on rent policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: critics of commodification (Benjamin on reproduction, the culture-industry critique) might favour free circulation of works, but the tradition never took a stand on patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Frankfurt School work on authoritarianism and the culture industry treats drilled, uniformed mass organisation as a mechanism of domination.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's anti-militarist, anti-domination stance; nuclear weapons were rarely addressed directly.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist, anti-militarist leanings; no direct treatment of foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from Adorno-era emphasis on memory of Auschwitz and confronting historical atrocity; no specific statement on state recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The tradition inherits Marx's critique that capital's returns derive from exploiting labour, which Lukács and Marcuse take as the basis of reification and domination.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Marxists generally accept defensive force and the tradition does not adopt pacifism, though some critics were wary of violence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its critique of ideology, which treats national myths as constructed and historically specific.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's critique of the 'naturalised' as socially produced, as reification theory argues, though it did not address sex directly.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the tradition wrote little on feminist identity politics, and later critical theorists split between universal and plural subjects.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its critique of myth and sacralised sacrifice, which it associates with authoritarian mobilisation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: it treats politics as shaped by domination, ideology and class interests, though Benjamin's messianic thought is a minority exception.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is internationalist and neither affirms nor rejects diaspora-homeland ideas.

culture-before-state.rationale: Gramsci's cultural hegemony puts cultural struggle before seizing the state, but the statement concerns national renewal, which the tradition did not address.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: the secular tradition did not address religious language, though Benjamin and Bloch drew on theological themes.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the tradition judges religion as ideology or as a source of utopia, but has no common stance on a women's-humanity test.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and critique of nationalism and group-based economic exclusion.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is internationalist and offers no case for ethnically defined regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Western Marxists distrusted bureaucratised institutions and valued working-class self-organisation; inferred, as unions were rarely their focus.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Lukács and Gramsci made working-class consciousness and self-rule central to socialism, and the tradition criticised Soviet party-state rule.

local-essentials-public.rationale: As anti-capitalists they would favour decommodified public provision; inferred, since they wrote little on policy.

second-chamber.rationale: The tradition had no stated view on parliamentary design, and council-minded thinkers differ from liberal-democratic reformers.

municipal-property.rationale: Gramsci and Korsch favoured workers' councils, which leans toward communal control, but the Frankfurt School said little; the strand is split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Council-oriented thinkers like Gramsci and Korsch sit close to it, but Frankfurt theorists did not develop such institutions; split.

family-wage.rationale: Their critique of wage labour and the culture of the patriarchal family (Frankfurt studies of authority) gives no clear stance on wage policy.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the critique of instrumental reason and of profit-driven science pulls one way and health gains the other.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Marcuse-style criticism of technological rationality conflicts with support for emancipatory use of science, so adherents are split; inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: They criticised administration and surveillance (s4) but also commodity exchange; there is no clear inference.

online-anonymity.rationale: Marcuse and the Frankfurt School warned of administered, surveilled society and defended individual autonomy; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Western Marxism rests on humanist Marx and the critique of domination and reification, rejecting subordination of persons to administrative wholes.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Some, like Benjamin and Bloch, drew on theological and utopian themes, while others stayed strictly materialist; the strand is split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Constitutional design of this kind was not a concern of the tradition; inferred neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: The critique of technological rationality and domination over nature suggests distrust of corporate biotechnology; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Lefebvre wrote on the city, but environmental claims about density were not part of the tradition; neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The tradition is class-centred and the Frankfurt School studied racism as pathology, so organising by race is not its framework; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Frankfurt studies of authoritarian personality treat group pride as a source of prejudice; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Critical theorists opposed militarism and aggressive wars (such as Vietnam); inferred from the critique of domination.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Western Marxists treated nations as historically produced and subordinate to class; inferred from this class-first outlook, they would reject language as a defining criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from a commitment to class solidarity across communities; separate religious electorates would be seen as fragmenting class consciousness, though the tradition did not address the question.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the tradition analyses domination through capital and ideology rather than national conspiracies, and Gramsci-style hegemony analysis treats such narratives as ideological.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and the critique of commodified culture; Marcuse and Gramsci valued education for the working class, though Marcuse also doubted that institutions integrated into the system liberate.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Marcuse and Adorno criticised domination of nature and the market logic of reification, so pricing pollution as the main tool would look like treating the symptom within the market order.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the Frankfurt critique of the domination of nature and instrumental reason, which implies concern for the conditions of future life.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marcuse linked feminism to a nonviolent, caring society, but the tradition mostly treats gender as socially constructed, so adherents are split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is critical of militarism and the repressive state, and Marcuse condemned the arms-driven affluent society, though it gave no program of arms agreements.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the demand for transparency and critique of administrative domination; the tradition did not address treaty secrecy directly.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism: adherents would favour public limits on capital, though they focused on culture and consciousness rather than policy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; the strand is split between critiquing the state and valuing the protection of order.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: Lukács and the Frankfurt thinkers opposed imperialist war, but wrote little on individual refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: collective workers' organisation fits its thought, though Marcuse saw unions as integrated into the system.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Marcuse-style critics saw welfare top-ups as managing and integrating workers, not changing the system.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: as anti-capitalists they oppose rules that limit public action in favour of markets.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism; the strand focused on culture and consciousness in the West and wrote little on this.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The strand is split: Lukács and Korsch favoured revolution, while Gramsci's war of position works through civil society and existing institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it rejects a single dogmatic blueprint and the Soviet model, but the sources do not state this.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Reification and the commodity form lead the strand to criticise pricing everything, and the Frankfurt School criticises instrumental reason applied to nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from its critique of ideology and domination; the Frankfurt School analysed nationalism as a source of authoritarianism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: it opposes the market's domination of life, but the sources do not discuss student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand focuses on class and culture, not regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The strand is split between the humanist Marx of species-being and the view that human nature is historically produced.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the culture industry critique opposes commercial control of media, and Habermas's public sphere supports independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Thinkers split: most were secular critics of religion, while Benjamin and Bloch drew on theology; inferred as split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism, which favours shielding producers from market forces, though the tradition seldom discussed agriculture.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Frankfurt School criticism of technological domination and militarised society; not a stated theme.

workers-own-party.rationale: The strand splits: Lukács and Gramsci defend a party, while Frankfurt thinkers distrust parties and see workers as integrated into the order.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from opposition to domination and the Frankfurt School's universalist ethics; the sources do not discuss FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's egalitarianism and critique of patriarchal domination; not a stated theme.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism, which looks to collective or democratic control rather than private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its critique of traditional authority and its democratic, emancipatory aims.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Marcuse linked domination of nature and people, but the tradition is wary of both ecological and state coercion; inferred as split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its critique of repressive state power and authoritarian character.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Western Marxists value strong collective workers' organisation and see compulsory dues as a protection against free-riding; inferred, with strands varying.

voter-id.rationale: The tradition treats formal electoral rules as bourgeois forms and would oppose barriers to participation; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Critical theorists favoured secular pluralism and no state privilege for any creed; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The tradition argues that formal elections within a capitalist order give little real freedom, and Marcuse's critique holds democracy needs substantive equality and autonomy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Critical theory, especially Marcuse and the Freudo-Marxists, favoured sexual liberation against repression.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition's concern with domination and free communication implies opposition to state cutoffs; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the tradition criticises capitalist welfare as integrating workers, and a market-style cash transfer would not replace socialised provision; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights are a basic emancipatory demand in the Marxist tradition, and nothing in the strand dissents.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxist critique of religion as ideology applies, but Western Marxists put more weight on capital and patriarchy than on religion; adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Critical theory treats categories as socially produced and historically shaped, and later Frankfurt thinkers analysed racism as ideology; inferred from that approach.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Adherents would accept state machinery for equality while doubting its reach under capitalism; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Social relations under capitalism take the form of relations between things, so people come to treat the market order as natural and unchangeable.
missingStatements.rationale: Reification is the central concept of Lukács's History and Class Consciousness and was extended by the Frankfurt School.

missingStatements.text: Working-class people in advanced capitalist societies have largely been integrated into the existing order and no longer form a revolutionary force.
missingStatements.rationale: Marcuse argues the technological work-world weakens the working class's negative position, and the SEP notes Frankfurt theorists saw workers lacking revolutionary consciousness.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow Frankfurt-school thesis, held at only medium strength; vanguard-party and labor-aristocracy already probe the working class's revolutionary role.

missingStatements.text: Reason applied only to controlling nature and people becomes an instrument of domination rather than liberation.
missingStatements.rationale: Dialectic of Enlightenment argues Enlightenment reason reverts to domination through instrumental rationality.

notes: The tradition is heterogeneous: Lukács and Gramsci were party communists, the Frankfurt School rejected both social democracy and Moscow, and Habermas is a liberal-democratic reformer. Many answers are medium or low because the sources seldom address concrete policy; neutral answers mark real splits within the strand.
